subject: music

moments.title: Phonograph invented
moments.body:
Edison's tinfoil cylinder recorder reproduces sound for the first time.

The technology will reshape both the music industry and how musical performance is studied.
moments.takeaway: Sound preservation began as a side-project in a research laboratory.

moments.title: Long-playing record
moments.body:
Peter Goldmark's 33 1/3 rpm vinyl LP holds about 22 minutes per side.

Longer forms (symphonies, jazz suites) are now sellable as complete works.
moments.takeaway: Media formats constrain and enable musical structures.

moments.title: Spotify launches
moments.body:
The streaming service launches in Europe, reaching the US in 2011.

The rise of streaming reorganises industry revenue around per-stream royalties.
moments.takeaway: Distribution technology continues to reshape musical economics.

now.title: Recorded music today
now.body: Recorded music revenues are mostly streaming. Cassette and vinyl re-emerged as smaller markets in the late 2010s. AI-generated music raises new attribution questions.
now.open_questions: What rights frameworks suit AI training on copyrighted recordings? How will live performance economics evolve?

reflection: Music's relationship to recording technology has been continuously renegotiated for nearly 150 years.
